applicableAreas: Western property boundary street yard area
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) at 1"=20' scale shows proposed trees (marked with 'M' and 'ST' symbols indicating mitigation and street yard trees) positioned directly overlapping or immediately adjacent to the underground electric line marked '-E-' running along the western property boundary. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) confirms underground electric lines route along this boundary. The vision analysis explicitly stated: 'Several tree symbols (tagged 'M' and 'ST') are drawn physically overlapping or immediately adjacent to the '-E-' line. Based on the 1"=20' scale, these proposed trees appear to be placed directly on top of, or within 5 feet of, this underground line.' This indicates violation of the 0-5 foot no-tree zone required for underground electric equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits any trees within 5 lateral feet of underground electric equipment (conduits, duct banks, cables, vaults, manholes, transformers). The landscape plan shows trees positioned directly over or immediately adjacent to the documented underground electric line. The visual positioning demonstrated in the plan drawings indicates non-compliance with the absolute 5-foot clearance requirement. This is not a case of approximate positioning that could be verified in the field—the plan itself shows the violation.
findings.comment: Proposed trees on the western property boundary are positioned directly on or within 5 lateral feet of the underground electric line. Remove trees from this zone or relocate the underground electric line to achieve minimum 5-foot clearance.

applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 5-20 feet of underground electric equipment
findings.observation: Sheet 31 shows proposed trees and shrubs throughout the site near underground electric infrastructure. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) provides standard tree planting details (Standard 610S-4 protection detail, tree planting pit specifications) but contains no root barrier construction details meeting UCM § 1.10.10.4 requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from equipment edge). The plant list on Sheet 35 identifies 12 trees being planted throughout the property near electric facilities, but no detail sheets show root barrier specifications coordinated with underground electric locations. The only root-related details on Sheet 37 describe tree protection during construction and standard planting practices, not UCM-compliant root barriers for electrical equipment protection.
findings.reasoning: For trees planted between 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment, UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers minimum 4 feet deep, positioned exactly 5 feet from the equipment edge. The landscape documentation does not provide these specific root barrier details for any trees positioned in this clearance zone. Standard tree planting details do not satisfy the specialized root barrier requirement for proximity to electrical infrastructure. The lack of any reference to UCM root barrier specifications in the landscape notes or details indicates non-compliance.
findings.comment: Provide root barrier construction details (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment edge) for all trees planted within 5-20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. Include typical cross-sections on detail sheets and cross-reference on landscape plan.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations throughout site (5 pads identified on Sheet 21)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads positioned at specific locations: adjacent to Bldg. 1 (near entrance), adjacent to Bldg. 2, in courtyard between Bldgs. 4/5, in courtyard between Bldgs. 6/7, and adjacent to Bldg. 8. However, Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show these transformer pad locations or their 10-foot clearance zones. The landscape plan shows multiple proposed trees throughout the site without reference to transformer locations, making it impossible to verify that trees are kept outside the 10-foot minimum clearance zone required by UCM § 1.10.10.4.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted transformers or electric equipment. The applicant must demonstrate compliance by showing transformer locations and clearance zones on the landscape plan. The absence of transformer pads on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided the minimum required documentation to verify compliance. This is a coordination failure between electrical design and landscape design.
findings.comment: Overlay transformer pad locations (from Sheet 21) on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and show 10-foot clearance zone around each pad. Verify all proposed trees and shrubs are outside these zones, or obtain Austin Energy written approval for any trees within this clearance.

findings.observation: The property plat (Sheet 2) and facts.md document record that electric easements exist on the property, including plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements. Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 20) explicitly states: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' However, the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show transmission easement boundaries, preventing verification that no trees are planted within transmission easements. Without visible easement boundaries overlaid on the landscape plan, compliance with the absolute prohibition on trees within transmission easements cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits all trees from being planted within electric transmission easements (facilities ≥60kV phase-to-phase). This is an absolute requirement with no exceptions based on tree size or species. The site plan notes on Sheet 3 reiterate this requirement. The applicant must show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan and demonstrate that no trees are positioned within them. The absence of easement boundaries on the landscape plan constitutes non-compliance with the documentation requirement.
findings.comment: Show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan. Verify and document that no proposed trees or shrubs are located within transmission easement areas. If any trees currently exist within transmission easements, indicate their removal or obtain Austin Energy written approval.

findings.observation: Review of all available site plan documents and supplementary documents (including Master Comment Report) reveals no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement for landscaping, trees, or irrigation within electric easement areas. The Master Comment Report (Electric Review section) references Austin Energy preliminary design requirements including UCM § 1.10.10.3, which requires a License Agreement before installing landscaping in electric easement areas. No such agreement is attached to the plans, referenced in any plan notes, or mentioned in any accompanying documentation. Sheet 31 shows trees proposed in areas where electric easements exist (per property records), but there is no evidence of the required license agreement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 explicitly requires that 'a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings that might obstruct access to Austin Energy facilities within electric easement areas. The agreement must be obtained and filed before the activity occurs.' The absence of this license agreement documentation on or with the site plan is a deficiency. While license agreements are administrative documents that may be obtained after plan approval, the applicant must provide evidence that the requirement has been addressed (or provide the executed agreement).
findings.comment: Obtain a License Agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement before installing any landscaping, trees, irrigation, or plantings within electric easement areas. Provide executed copy with final site plan submittal or reference execution in a plan note.

applicableAreas: Utility pole locations along street right-of-way
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows utility poles depicted as small circles with crosshairs located along the far left edge of the property along the street right-of-way. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these utility pole locations. Without the pole locations shown on the landscape plan, there is no means to verify that proposed trees maintain the required 10-foot minimum clearance from poles.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires that no trees be planted within 10 lateral feet of electric utility poles. The landscape plan must show pole locations to enable verification of compliance. The absence of pole locations on the landscape plan means the applicant has not provided sufficient documentation to verify this clearance requirement.
findings.comment: Identify and show utility pole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones around each pole and verify all proposed trees are outside these zones.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads with their locations but does not clearly indicate access door orientations. Sheet 31 shows shrubs and low vegetation symbols throughout the site (marked PM=Dwarf Palmetto, MB=Big Muhly, GC=Gulf Muhly, LS=Texas Sage, MC=Dwarf Wax Myrtle per Sheet 35) but does not show transformer pad locations or access door sides to verify 10-foot clearance.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that no shrubs be planted within 10 lateral feet of the access door side (hot-stick-use area/pad-locked side) of pad-mounted equipment. Without transformer locations and their access door orientations shown on the landscape plan, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance.
findings.comment: Show transformer pad locations and access door orientations on the landscape plan. Mark 10-foot clearance zones on access door sides and verify no shrubs are positioned within these zones.

findings.observation: Same as EL-16.15: transformer pad locations and orientations not shown on landscape plan, preventing verification of 5-foot shrub clearance on non-access sides.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 5-foot clearance from non-access sides of pad-mounted equipment. Landscape plan must show transformer locations and orientations to verify this clearance.
findings.comment: Show transformer pad locations and identify access vs. non-access sides on the landscape plan. Verify shrubs are at least 5 feet from non-access sides.

applicableAreas: Subsurface electric vaults and manhole locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows vault and manhole locations (including a labeled 'Vault Easement' at transformer pad near Bldg. 8). Sheet 31 does not show these vault/manhole locations. Without them overlaid on the landscape plan, the required 8-foot clearance zone around vaults/manholes cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access. The landscape plan must show vault/manhole locations to enable verification.
findings.comment: Show vault and manhole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 8-foot clearance zones around each vault/manhole requiring personnel access and verify shrubs and obstructions are outside these zones.

applicableAreas: Space between transformer access doors and drivable surfaces
findings.observation: Transformer pad locations not shown on landscape plan, preventing verification of tree-free access routes from transformer access doors to drivable surfaces (streets, alleys, parking areas).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees between the access door of pad-mounted equipment and drivable surfaces used for truck access. This zone must remain clear for bucket truck positioning during hot-stick work. Verification requires transformer locations and access routes to be shown on the landscape plan.
findings.comment: Show transformer locations and identify access doors on the landscape plan. Verify that no trees block the route from each transformer access door to the nearest drivable surface (street, alley, or parking area).

applicableAreas: Transformer locations and access routes throughout site
findings.observation: Transformer pad locations from Sheet 21 and access routes from Sheet 9 (Site Plan) are not overlaid on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Without this coordination, it cannot be verified that proposed trees do not obstruct access routes or turning radii for bucket trucks used to service transformers and Austin Energy equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping must not restrict Austin Energy personnel and equipment access. The landscape plan must show transformer locations and access requirements to demonstrate compliance. The absence of this coordination indicates non-compliance with the access requirement.
findings.comment: Show transformer locations and required truck access routes on the landscape plan. Verify no trees block access lanes or turning radii required for Austin Energy service vehicles (typical 40-50 ft turning radius for bucket trucks).

findings.observation: Vault locations shown on Sheet 21 are not shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vault covers/lids must remain clear of tree canopy for operational access, but without vault locations on the landscape plan, this cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires that vaults remain accessible for personnel and equipment. Trees positioned over vault covers prevent access operations. The landscape plan must show vault locations and tree canopy spreads to verify compliance.
findings.comment: Show vault locations on the landscape plan with tree locations and estimated mature canopy spreads. Verify no trees are positioned to create overhead obstruction of vault covers/lids.

applicableAreas: Entire site - all utility and landscape areas
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows all electric facilities: transformer pads, underground electric lines (marked '-E-'), pull boxes, meter banks, utility poles, vault easement, and various utility easements. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any of these electric facilities. The landscape plan shows only landscape elements (trees, shrubs, paving, contours, irrigation notes) without any reference to electrical infrastructure locations. This prevents all clearance verifications required by checklist items EL-16.1 through EL-16.21.
findings.reasoning: Proper coordination between electrical and landscape design requires that electric facilities be shown on the landscape plan at the same scale. This allows visual verification of clearance zones, easement boundaries, and access routes. The absence of electrical infrastructure on the landscape plan is a fundamental coordination failure that prevents the reviewer from verifying compliance with any of the electric facility proximity requirements. This is not optional—it is a standard requirement for site plan review.
findings.comment: Overlay all electric facilities from Sheet 21 onto the landscape plan (Sheet 31), including transformer pads, underground electric lines (with 5-foot and broader clearance zones clearly marked), pull boxes, utility poles, vault locations, electric easement boundaries, and transmission easement boundaries. This overlay is essential for verifying compliance with all vegetation clearance requirements.
